meta.title: The man who chose to suffer on purpose

beats.text: "I am a sick man. I am a spiteful man. I am an unattractive man."
So begins Dostoevsky's Notes from Underground — the diary of a man who hides from the world.
For forty years he has stewed in a cramped room, despising everyone, himself most of all.
He attacks a comforting idea: that if we only knew our own good, we would always choose it.
No, he says. A man will choose pain, ruin, and spite just to prove he is free — not a piano key.
We would rather suffer as ourselves than be happy as a cog in someone else's reason.
It is ugly, and it is honest — which is exactly why we still read him.

source_note: Quote: Notes from Underground, trans. Constance Garnett (1918, public domain).
